Code is TensorFlow 1.x (tf.placeholder, tf.Session, slim, tf.variable_scope), gym CartPole-v0/Breakout-v0, scipy imresize: all dated and not runnable on current stacks.

Code has bugs: calculate_naive_returns loops over range(len(rewards), 0) which is empty and uses an undefined name; the PG 'solved' check slices episode_rewards[:-100] (the first, not last, 100) and runs when i % 10 is nonzero; DQN main sets solved False in both branches; ExperienceReplayTable.sample_batch returns discounted_returns as the terminal flag; annealing text says epsilon starts low and increases while code decreases it; PG policy loss multiplies by return with no baseline or normalisation.
The chapter's own text says build_model returns three action nodes, but CartPole has 2 actions.
Covers 2013-2016 methods only (DQN, A3C, UNREAL, DRQN); no PPO, TRPO, DDPG, SAC, double/dueling DQN, prioritised replay, or RLHF.
practices: Use discounted return with gamma 0.97 to 0.99 so agents value reward soon (p.251).
Anneal epsilon from high to low so the agent explores early and exploits late; fixed epsilon performed poorly (pp.253, 261).
Stabilise DQN with a lagged target network and experience replay with random sampling and eviction of old experience (pp.263-264).
Stack the last 4 frames as channels to give DQN velocity information; DRQN replaces this with a recurrent layer (pp.265, 273).
Use an advantage (R_t - V(s_t)) rather than raw return in actor-critic (p.275).

terms.definition: S, a finite set of possible states; A, a finite set of actions; P(r, s' | s, a), a state transition function; R, reward function
the way in which our agent acts based on its current state; a function pi that chooses the action a that the agent will take in state s
R_t = sum gamma^t r_{t+k+1}; gamma between 0 and 1, high gamma little discounting
Q(s,a) calculates the maximum discounted future return when action a is performed in state s
Q*(s_t,a_t) = E[r_t + gamma max_a' Q*(s_t+1, a')]
a copy of the prediction network that lags in its parameter updates
store all experiences as (s,a,r,s') tuples and sample batches at random to break correlation
A_t = Q*(s_t,a_t) - V(s_t); A3C approximates it as R_t - V(s_t)

code.snippet:
def discount_rewards(rewards, gamma=0.98):
    discounted_returns = [0 for _ in rewards]
    discounted_returns[-1] = rewards[-1]
    for t in range(len(rewards)-2, -1, -1): # iterate backwards
        discounted_returns[t] = rewards[t] + discounted_returns[t+1]*gamma
    return discounted_returns

min_theta sum_e sum_t ( Q(s_t,a_t|theta) - (r_t + gamma max_a' Q(s_t+1,a'|theta)) )
